newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis sees clear rise in 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Novartis sees clear rise in 1997 profit.

text.p: Novartis AG on Tuesday reported a 1996 net profit of 2.30 billion Swiss francs ($1.6 billion), down from 4.22 billion in 1995.
Excluding exceptional items, 1996 net rose two percent to 4.18 billion from 4.10 billion.
Novartis, formed by the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG last year, also said in a statement it expected most of its integration projects to be finished this year.
The company predicted that that operating profit and net profit would grow markedly in 1997, but it did not give a specific forecast.

"Implementaation of the merger is progressing well, with the majority of integration projects expected to be completed in 1997. In parallel, growth of established key products continues to be strong and new, innovative products are rapidly increasing their importance thanks to an aggressive programme of product launches already under way," the statement said.

"We anticipate a continued upward trend in top-line growth, with sales across all sectors and in most regions expected to grow dynamically. In 1997, we should also experience a strong positive currency effect. Together with the realisation of the merger synthesis, this should lead, barring any unforeseen events, to a marked improvement of operating and net income."
